analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of understanding about the impact of post-viral sequelae, specifically long COVID and post-viral fatigue syndrome (PVFS), on children and young people's (CYP) primary care use.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective, population-based dynamic cohort study was conducted using Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum data for CYP aged <18 years in England, between 1st January 2006 and 31st December 2022, with a focus on the period from 1st March 2020 onwards for long COVID.
analysis.methods: Negative binomial regression was used to estimate associations between sociodemographic characteristics and consultation rates for long COVID and PVFS.
analysis.main_results: The study found 6700 long COVID and 20,440 PVFS consultations. Long COVID consultation rates were highest in 2022 at 140.3 per 100,000 child-years, while PVFS consultation rates peaked in 2009 and 2022 at 57.1 and 56.9 per 100,000 child-years, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the highest consultation rates for long COVID and PVFS were observed during the pandemic and the H1N1 outbreak, and noted that the findings regarding higher rates in less deprived areas and among girls require further investigation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance and resource allocation in primary care for post-viral conditions, particularly during influenza pandemics, highlighting the need for targeted support in specific sociodemographic groups.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on existing data, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations and the focus on observed consultation rates without causal analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines trends in long COVID and post-viral fatigue syndrome (PVFS) consultations in children and young people (CYP) in England between 2006 and 2022. It highlights that long COVID consultation rates were highest in 2022, while PVFS rates peaked during the 2009 H1N1 pandemic and the 2022 COVID-19 pandemic. The research identifies higher consultation rates among older CYP, girls, and those from less deprived areas, suggesting potential sociodemographic patterns. The study's findings are relevant for understanding the impact of post-viral conditions on primary care use and may guide future surveillance and resource allocation. However, the retrospective design and reliance on existing data limit the confidence in the results, leading to a moderate evidence assessment.

title: Influenza A H1N1 Infection Triggers Endothelial Immunothrombosis via TNF-α–Tissue Factor–Thrombin Signaling in Human Brain Microvascular Endothelial Cells
abstract: Severe Influenza A virus (IAV) infection is associated with endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and coagulation abnormalities. However, the mechanisms linking endothelial inflammatory activation to thrombosis remain incompletely understood. We investigated whether Influenza A/H1N1 induces an immunothrombotic phenotype in human brain microvascular endothelial cells. We infected HBEC-5i cells with Influenza A/H1N1 pdm09. We assessed viral infection by RT-qPCR detection of matrix (M) transcripts and by immunoblotting for the M1 protein. We evaluated endothelial responses by measuring TNF-α expression and secretion, Tissue Factor (TF) expression, TF-dependent factor Xa generation, and responses to recombinant TNF-α and thrombin. H1N1 infection increased TNF-α expression and secretion and enhanced TF expression and functional activity, indicating acquisition of a procoagulant endothelial phenotype. Recombinant TNF-α reproduced infection-associated TF induction, whereas thrombin enhanced TNF-α production and TF activity, supporting reciprocal amplification between inflammatory and coagulation pathways. These findings support a TNF-α–TF–thrombin feed-forward signaling circuit linking endothelial inflammation and coagulation during H1N1 infection. Influenza A/H1N1 induces an immunothrombotic phenotype in human brain microvascular endothelial cells, identifying this signaling axis as a potential mechanistic target for influenza-associated vascular and thrombotic complications.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 严重的流感A病毒(IAV)感染与内皮功能障碍、炎症和凝血异常有关。然而,将内皮炎症激活与血栓形成联系起来的机制仍不完全清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们研究了流感A/H1N1是否在人类脑微血管内皮细胞中诱导免疫血栓表型。
elements_zh.methods: 我们用流感A/H1N1 pdm09感染HBEC-5i细胞,并通过RT-qPCR检测基质(M)转录物和通过免疫印迹检测M1蛋白来评估病毒感染。我们通过测量TNF-α表达和分泌、组织因子(TF)表达、TF依赖的因子Xa生成以及对重组TNF-α和凝血酶的反应来评估内皮反应。
elements_zh.main_results: H1N1 感染增加了 TNF-α 的表达和分泌,并增强了 TF 的表达和功能活性,表明获得了促凝血内皮表型。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现支持了一个TNF-α–TF–凝血酶的正反馈信号通路,将H1N1感染期间的内皮炎症与凝血联系起来。流感A/H1N1在人类脑微血管内皮细胞中诱导免疫血栓表型,这表明该信号轴可能是流感相关血管和血栓并发症的潜在机制靶点。

title_zh: 甲型 H1N1 流感感染通过人脑微血管内皮细胞中的 TNF-α-组织因子-凝血酶信号触发内皮免疫血栓形成
source_body_en: Severe Influenza A virus (IAV) infection is associated with endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and coagulation abnormalities. However, the mechanisms linking endothelial inflammatory activation to thrombosis remain incompletely understood. We investigated whether Influenza A/H1N1 induces an immunothrombotic phenotype in human brain microvascular endothelial cells. We infected HBEC-5i cells with Influenza A/H1N1 pdm09. We assessed viral infection by RT-qPCR detection of matrix (M) transcripts and by immunoblotting for the M1 protein. We evaluated endothelial responses by measuring TNF-α expression and secretion, Tissue Factor (TF) expression, TF-dependent factor Xa generation, and responses to recombinant TNF-α and thrombin. H1N1 infection increased TNF-α expression and secretion and enhanced TF expression and functional activity, indicating acquisition of a procoagulant endothelial phenotype. Recombinant TNF-α reproduced infection-associated TF induction, whereas thrombin enhanced TNF-α production and TF activity, supporting reciprocal amplification between inflammatory and coagulation pathways. These findings support a TNF-α–TF–thrombin feed-forward signaling circuit linking endothelial inflammation and coagulation during H1N1 infection. Influenza A/H1N1 induces an immunothrombotic phenotype in human brain microvascular endothelial cells, identifying this signaling axis as a potential mechanistic target for influenza-associated vascular and thrombotic complications.
abstract_zh: 严重甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 感染与内皮功能障碍、炎症和凝血异常有关。然而,内皮炎症激活与血栓形成之间的联系机制仍不完全清楚。我们研究了甲型 H1N1 流感是否会在人脑微血管内皮细胞中诱导免疫血栓表型。我们用甲型流感/H1N1 pdm09 感染 HBEC-5i 细胞。我们通过 RT-qPCR 检测基质 (M) 转录物和 M1 蛋白的免疫印迹来评估病毒感染。我们通过测量 TNF-α 表达和分泌、组织因子 (TF) 表达、TF 依赖性因子 Xa 生成以及对重组 TNF-α 和凝血酶的反应来评估内皮反应。H1N1 感染增加了 TNF-α 的表达和分泌,并增强了 TF 的表达和功能活性,表明获得了促凝血内皮表型。重组 TNF-α 再现了感染相关的 TF 诱导,而凝血酶增强了 TNF-α 的产生和 TF 活性,支持炎症和凝血途径之间的相互放大。这些发现支持 TNF-α-TF-凝血酶前馈信号回路在 H1N1 感染期间将内皮炎症和凝血联系起来。甲型 H1N1 流感在人脑微血管内皮细胞中诱导免疫血栓表型,将该信号轴确定为流感相关血管和血栓并发症的潜在机制靶点。

title: Clinical Relevance of Multiplex PCR for Respiratory Pathogens in Hospitalized Adults with Influenza-Like Illness
abstract: Objective: Influenza-like illness (ILI) is a major cause of hospitalization during respiratory virus seasons. This study aimed to investigate the pathogens detected in patients presenting with ILI symptoms and to analyze the results in conjunction with clinical, laboratory, and radiological findings. Materials and Methods: This retrospective, single-center study included 446 hospitalized adults with ILI between epidemiological week 40 of 2024 and week 20 of 2025. Respiratory pathogens were identified using a multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assay detecting 18 viral and 5 bacterial pathogens. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and radiological data were retrieved from electronic medical records. Disease severity was assessed using the CURB-65 score. Patients with Streptococcus pneumoniae detected by PCR were further evaluated according to radiological evidence of pneumonia. Results: At least one respiratory pathogen was detected in 184/446 patients (41.2%), whereas no pathogen was identified in 262 patients (58.8%). The most frequently detected pathogens were S. pneumoniae, influenza viruses, and seasonal coronaviruses. The most common coinfection was influenza A plus S. Among patients with pneumococcal PCR positivity, those with radiologically confirmed pneumonia were significantly older, had higher CURB-65 scores, and more frequently had concomitant influenza infection than patients without radiological evidence of pneumonia. Conclusion: Multiplex molecular assays provide valuable information for respiratory pathogen detection, but molecular results, especially for bacterial pathogens such as S. pneumoniae, should be interpreted together with clinical and radiological findings.
journal: Journal of Clinical Practice and Research

title: Parental Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Toward Influenza Vaccine Uptake Among Children in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background: Seasonal influenza is a major public health concern, particularly among children who are at high risk of infection and can transmit the virus to others. Vaccination is the primary preventive measure. Parental knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) may influence vaccination decisions. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among Saudi parents attending primary healthcare centers in Jeddah. Parents with at least one child aged six months or older were eligible. Data were collected using a validated self-administered Arabic questionnaire assessing knowledge, attitudes, awareness, perceived barriers, and vaccine uptake. Descriptive statistics and chi-square tests were used to examine associations, and binary logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors of vaccine uptake. Results: A total of 308 parents participated. Influenza vaccine uptake was reported by 57.5% of participants. Nearly all participants (97.7%) demonstrated good knowledge, but the knowledge score was not significantly associated with vaccine uptake (p = 0.399). Parental attitude was a significant independent predictor (OR = 1.090, 95% CI: 1.033-1.149, p = 0.001). Education level was also significantly associated with uptake (p = 0.015), with lower-educated parents showing higher odds of vaccination compared to postgraduate-educated parents. Exposure to awareness campaigns was significantly associated with higher uptake (p < 0.001). The most reported barriers were the belief that vaccination was unnecessary (9.4%) and concerns about side effects (8.4%), both strongly associated with non-vaccination (p < 0.001). Conclusion: Although most parents had good knowledge about influenza vaccination, this did not translate into consistent vaccination behavior. Parental attitudes and awareness campaign exposure were the main predictors of vaccine uptake. Public health strategies should shift from broad factual dissemination to targeted, point-of-care counseling that addresses misconceptions about vaccine necessity and safety to improve influenza vaccination rates among children in Saudi Arabia.

elements_zh.methods: 使用描述性统计和卡方检验分析相关性,并通过二元逻辑回归确定疫苗接种的独立预测因素。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 尽管大多数父母对流感疫苗接种有良好的知识,但这并未转化为一致的疫苗接种行为。父母的态度和宣传运动的接触是疫苗接种的主要预测因素。

Conclusion: Although most parents had good knowledge about influenza vaccination, this did not translate into consistent vaccination behavior. Parental attitudes and awareness campaign exposure were the main predictors of vaccine uptake. Public health strategies should shift from broad factual dissemination to targeted, point-of-care counseling that addresses misconceptions about vaccine necessity and safety to improve influenza vaccination rates among children in Saudi Arabia.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 流感疫苗接种是重要的公共卫生问题,尤其是对儿童而言,他们感染风险较高且可能将病毒传播给他人。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 在沙特阿拉伯吉达市的初级卫生保健中心,对参加活动的父母进行横断面研究。至少有一个6个月以上儿童的父母有资格参与。数据通过经过验证的自填阿拉伯语问卷收集,评估知识、态度、意识、感知障碍和疫苗接种情况。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用描述性统计和卡方检验分析相关性,并通过二元逻辑回归确定疫苗接种的独立预测因素。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 尽管大多数父母对流感疫苗接种有良好的知识,但这并未转化为一致的疫苗接种行为。父母的态度和宣传运动的接触是疫苗接种的主要预测因素。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 公共卫生策略应从广泛的事实传播转向有针对性的、现场咨询,以解决对疫苗接种必要性和安全性的误解,从而提高沙特阿拉伯儿童的流感疫苗接种率。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告该研究的局限性。

title: Editorial: Measuring vaccination perception, confidence, and uptake: advancing instrument development and validation
abstract: Two contributions in this Research Topic directly advance the measurement science that motivated this Topic. ground the development of a new general measure of adult vaccine hesitancy for U.S. adults in the 3C framework, reporting content and face validity findings, including a content validity index derived from expert panel review, for an instrument intended to capture hesitancy across vaccine types rather than a single indication. report the development and psychometric evaluation of the Vaccine Hesitancy and Perception Scale toward COVID-19 vaccination (VHAPS-CV19), employing principal axis factoring with varimax rotation to derive a two-factor structure that distinguishes a hesitancy factor (confidence, complacency, and convenience) from a perception-and-trust factor (perceived benefit, barrier, susceptibility, severity, and trust), together with internal consistency estimates for each subscale. Together, the two studies trace the stages that valid measurement of a construct this complex demands, from item generation and content validity through factor structure and reliability testing, and they leave the field with two complementary tools, one general-purpose and one vaccine-specific, for future validation and cross-cultural adaptation work.Several contributions in this Topic examine hesitancy and uptake among healthcare workers, a population whose own vaccination behavior and patient communication directly shape public confidence. investigated uptake, willingness, and practices toward seasonal influenza vaccination among healthcare workers in China using a cross-sectional design. similarly employed a cross-sectional survey to explore attitudes toward COVID-19 vaccination among healthcare workers at a national infectious disease center in Singapore, while Aksoy et al. surveyed community pharmacists in Türkiye regarding their knowledge, attitudes, and barriers toward vaccination, extending the focus to frontline advocates outside the hospital setting. took a distinct, qualitative approach, interviewing healthcare workers at a London hospital to identify barriers and facilitators to measles vaccination uptake; this design complements the quantitative work elsewhere in the Topic, surfacing workplace, informational, and interpersonal factors that structured surveys tend to miss.A second cluster of contributions addresses hesitancy and uptake determinants in community and general-population samples, extending the scope of this Topic beyond influenza and COVID-19 to additional vaccine types and life stages. Rounding out the collection, Ali et al. provide a narrative review of enablers and barriers to influenza vaccine uptake among healthcare workers in Gulf Cooperation Council countries, synthesizing evidence from a regional context that is comparatively underrepresented in the vaccine hesitancy literature relative to North America, Europe, and East Asia. contribute a distinct but complementary perspective, presenting a multivariate analysis of risk factors for adverse events following rabies vaccination using real-world data. This work centers on vaccine safety rather than perception, but it is a reminder that confidence in vaccination rests on lived experience with tolerability as much as on attitudes and access, and that perception-focused instruments are best read alongside pharmacovigilance data.A few patterns stand out across this collection (Figure 1; Table 1). Geographically, contributions concentrate in China (six studies), with additional representation from the United States, Singapore, Türkiye, Vietnam, the United Kingdom, and the Gulf Cooperation Council region; populations in Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Latin America are absent, which limits how far these findings generalize and points to a direction for future Research Topics. Methodologically, most contributions rely on cross-sectional, self-report surveys. These designs are useful for generating hypotheses about correlates of hesitancy, but they cannot establish temporal precedence between attitude and behavior, and they remain vulnerable to social desirability and recall bias. Only one contribution employed qualitative interview methods, and none employed a longitudinal or experimental design; this concentration of designs mirrors the broader hesitancy literature and marks a gap that future work should close.Taken together, the contributions to this Research Topic make clear that vaccine decision-making has many layers. Hesitancy and confidence are shaped at once by individual psychology, professional role, cultural context, service accessibility, and direct experience with vaccine safety. The instrument development studies respond to a real methodological gap: the field needs measurement tools that are psychometrically sound and adaptable across populations. The determinant studies argue the opposite case for context. Findings from healthcare workers in the Gulf region, older adults in western China, and pharmacists in Türkiye are not interchangeable; each offers insight for the setting studied rather than a universal account of vaccine hesitancy.A few gaps remain for future research. Cross-cultural validation of the instruments introduced here, including measurement invariance testing and comparison against benchmarks such as the WHO SAGE Vaccine Hesitancy Scale (2), would strengthen confidence in their applicability across populations. Longitudinal designs tracking how measured hesitancy or confidence relates to actual vaccination behavior over time, rather than to intention alone, would help close the well-documented gap between attitudinal measurement and uptake outcomes. Greater use of qualitative and mixed-methods designs, alongside the cross-sectional surveys predominant here, would help clarify mechanisms that quantitative models identify but cannot fully explain. Finally, as vaccine platforms and communication environments evolve, measurement tools will need periodic re-validation to remain sensitive to emerging determinants of hesitancy.

The instrument development studies respond to a real methodological gap: the field needs measurement tools that are psychometrically sound and adaptable across populations. Findings from healthcare workers in the Gulf region, older adults in western China, and pharmacists in Türkiye are not interchangeable; each offers insight for the setting studied rather than a universal account of vaccine hesitancy.A few gaps remain for future research. Cross-cultural validation of the instruments introduced here, including measurement invariance testing and comparison against benchmarks such as the WHO SAGE Vaccine Hesitancy Scale (2), would strengthen confidence in their applicability across populations. Rounding out the collection, Ali et al. provide a narrative review of enablers and barriers to influenza vaccine uptake among healthcare workers in Gulf Cooperation Council countries, synthesizing evidence from a regional context that is comparatively underrepresented in the vaccine hesitancy literature relative to North America, Europe, and East Asia. contribute a distinct but complementary perspective, presenting a multivariate analysis of risk factors for adverse events following rabies vaccination using real-world data. This work centers on vaccine safety rather than perception, but it is a reminder that confidence in vaccination rests on lived experience with tolerability as much as on attitudes and access, and that perception-focused instruments are best read alongside pharmacovigilance data.A few patterns stand out across this collection (Figure 1; Table 1). Geographically, contributions concentrate in China (six studies), with additional representation from the United States, Singapore, Türkiye, Vietnam, the United Kingdom, and the Gulf Cooperation Council region; populations in Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Latin America are absent, which limits how far these findings generalize and points to a direction for future Research Topics. These designs are useful for generating hypotheses about correlates of hesitancy, but they cannot establish temporal precedence between attitude and behavior, and they remain vulnerable to social desirability and recall bias. Only one contribution employed qualitative interview methods, and none employed a longitudinal or experimental design; this concentration of designs mirrors the broader hesitancy literature and marks a gap that future work should close.Taken together, the contributions to this Research Topic make clear that vaccine decision-making has many layers. Hesitancy and confidence are shaped at once by individual psychology, professional role, cultural context, service accessibility, and direct experience with vaccine safety. The determinant studies argue the opposite case for context. Cross-cultural validation of the instruments introduced here, including measurement invariance testing and comparison against benchmarks such as the WHO SAGE Vaccine Hesitancy Scale (2), would strengthen confidence in their applicability across populations. title: Nowcasting officially reported highly pathogenic avian influenza outbreak counts under heterogeneous reporting delays
abstract: Official animal disease series are often incomplete due to delays in reporting. This retrospective observational study evaluated whether increased model complexity enhances probabilistic nowcasts of eventual officially reported outbreak-equivalent counts. We reconstructed historical information states from a fixed extraction from the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) World Animal Health Information System (WAHIS), which included 46,860 highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) and 72,690 African swine fever (ASF) outbreaks. Twelve prespecified methods were assessed over 78 locked cutoffs for 2024–2025 using the Weighted Interval Score (WIS), calibration diagnostics, block bootstrap, simulation, and a separately frozen USDA APHIS transfer evaluation. The primary HPAI analysis included 35,880 observations from 115 country–host units. At week closure, only 7.6% of eventual HPAI and 6.7% of ASF outbreak equivalents were visible, with completeness varying by host, region, year, season, and workload. The prespecified primary hypothesis was not supported: the delay-aware temporal network scored 6.9% worse than the hierarchical Bayesian comparator, and the relational graph changed WIS by only 0.4%. Gradient-boosted quantile regression improved WIS by 18.5% (absolute difference −0.0397, 95% interval −0.0553 to −0.0255), but the improvement reached 26.0% among high-volume reporters and reversed to a 6.3% deficit among units with minimal reporting history. Conditioning on the partial count was 24.7% worse than a matched no-delay network at cohort age 0 and performed better thereafter. The slower-reporting ASF system reversed the pooled contrast, whereas the APHIS module improved WIS by 10.1% after system-specific retraining. Adding an explicit mass at zero enhanced the transparent comparator by 18.8% and resulted in no detectable difference from gradient boosting; the neural model remained 17.4% worse under the same recalibration. In exploratory analyses, gradient boosting cleared the prespecified 5% gate under all six cohort definitions and all three maturity horizons. Performance deteriorated markedly for high-volume countries and regions excluded from training. These estimates pertain to eventual officially reported outbreak equivalents under the surveillance conditions studied, not undetected infections.

This retrospective observational study evaluated whether increased model complexity enhances probabilistic nowcasts of eventual officially reported outbreak-equivalent counts. We reconstructed historical information states from a fixed extraction from the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) World Animal Health Information System (WAHIS), which included 46,860 highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) and 72,690 African swine fever (ASF) outbreaks. Twelve prespecified methods were assessed over 78 locked cutoffs for 2024–2025 using the Weighted Interval Score (WIS), calibration diagnostics, block bootstrap, simulation, and a separately frozen USDA APHIS transfer evaluation. The primary HPAI analysis included 35,880 observations from 115 country–host units. At week closure, only 7.6% of eventual HPAI and 6.7% of ASF outbreak equivalents were visible, with completeness varying by host, region, year, season, and workload. The prespecified primary hypothesis was not supported: the delay-aware temporal network scored 6.9% worse than the hierarchical Bayesian comparator, and the relational graph changed WIS by only 0.4%. Gradient-boosted quantile regression improved WIS by 18.5% (absolute difference −0.0397, 95% interval −0.0553 to −0.0255), but the improvement reached 26.0% among high-volume reporters and reversed to a 6.3% deficit among units with minimal reporting history. Conditioning on the partial count was 24.7% worse than a matched no-delay network at cohort age 0 and performed better thereafter. The slower-reporting ASF system reversed the pooled contrast, whereas the APHIS module improved WIS by 10.1% after system-specific retraining. Adding an explicit mass at zero enhanced the transparent comparator by 18.8% and resulted in no detectable difference from gradient boosting; the neural model remained 17.4% worse under the same recalibration. In exploratory analyses, gradient boosting cleared the prespecified 5% gate under all six cohort definitions and all three maturity horizons. Performance deteriorated markedly for high-volume countries and regions excluded from training. These estimates pertain to eventual officially reported outbreak equivalents under the surveillance conditions studied, not undetected infections.

title: Influenza vaccination in childhood and adolescence. Evaluation of the 2025-2026 campaign in Spain and improvement strategies. Report by AEV, CAV-AEP and SEIP.
abstract: Seasonal influenza represents a significant burden in childhood. This article analyzes pediatric influenza vaccination during the 2025-2026 campaign, as well as epidemiological, effectiveness, and preliminary vaccination coverage data. Routine vaccination against influenza between ages 6 and 59 months, as well as the extension of the recommendation up to 17 years, as outlined in the 2025 AEV, CAV-AEP, and SEIP consensus document, is key to individual and collective protection. We propose advancing further in developing effective strategies to continue increasing vaccination coverage, as well as expanding the age range for vaccination, as has already been implemented in some autonomous communities in 2025-2026.

la Sociedad Española de Infectología Pediátrica (SEIP) y la Asociación Española de Vacunología (AEV)

The authors highlight the significant burden of seasonal influenza in childhood and emphasize the need for further strategies to increase vaccination coverage. They propose extending the age range for vaccination, as some autonomous communities have already implemented this change. The findings suggest that broadening vaccination recommendations could enhance protection against seasonal influenza. However, the evidence does not include specific limitations or a formal assessment of the study's strength.

title: Mice immunized with N1 neuraminidase in a single cycle infectious virus or in a recombinant nanoparticle vaccine are protected against lethal challenge with highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 influenza
abstract: The recent spillover of highly pathogenic (HP) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b into dairy cattle and other mammalian species has been concerning. Vaccine candidates that can be rapidly synthesized and implemented are key countermeasures for protecting the human population against emerging pathogens. Here we examine the use of a pH1N1 virus lacking the genetic material for hemagglutinin (HA), limiting the infection to a single cycle (sciIAV) or Cobalt lipid-porphyrin nanoparticles decorated with neuraminidase (NA) of HPAI H5N1 (N1-CoPoP) as vaccine candidates. C57BL/6 mice that were inoculated intranasally with a single dose of pH1N1 sciIAV did not differ in serum NA antibody compared to uninoculated mice. However, mice that were inoculated intramuscularly with the N1-CoPoP alone or in combination with pH1N1 sciIAV had increased N1 IgG antibodies. Upon lethal challenge with HPAIV H5N1, all mice inoculated with either pH1N1 sciIAV or N1-CoPoP were protected from weight loss, unlike unvaccinated mice with substantial body weight losses that succumb to viral infection between 7 and 10 days post infection (dpi). Both pH1N1 sciIAV and N1-CoPoP immunization minimized viral infection such that only one mouse receiving pH1N1 sciIAV had detectable viral titer in the lungs at 4 dpi. By 6 dpi, no mouse inoculated with pH1N1 sciIAV and/or N1-CoPoP had detectable virus in nasal turbinates, lungs or the brain, unlike the high viral titers found in uninoculated mice. Both pH1N1 sciIAV and N1-CoPoP were protective and should be investigated further as alternative vaccine candidates.

title: Highly pathogenic avian influenza as a systemic risk - implications for control and preparedness
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) has evolved from episodic outbreaks into a globally entrenched, multi-host panzootic, with recurrent spillover into mammals. The expanding host range and increasing wildlife–livestock interfaces challenge traditional control strategies, increase opportunities for viral adaptation, and thereby elevate zoonotic risk. We therefore propose that HPAI should be reframed as a long-term systemic risk requiring resilience-based governance, and strengthened One Health control and preparedness.

title: A territory-wide study on adults hospitalized for rhinovirus infection – mortality, severe adverse respiratory and renal outcomes and relationships with multiple comorbidities
abstract: While rhinovirus was thought to cause mild infections such as the common cold, severe infections such as community-acquired pneumonia and asthma exacerbations can also occur. Children with chronic medical conditions have been shown to have increased risks of severe infections. Hypothesis/Gap statement. There is a difference in the risks of serious in-hospital outcomes among adults hospitalized for rhinovirus or influenza virus infection. Multiple morbidities in adult patients are associated with severe infections among patients hospitalized for rhinovirus infections. To compare the risks of serious in-hospital outcomes among adults hospitalized for rhinovirus or influenza virus infection and assess the association between multiple morbidities as represented by Charlson comorbidity index (CCI) in predicting risks of severe infections among patients hospitalized for rhinovirus infections. We conducted a territory-wide retrospective study on adults hospitalized for rhinovirus or influenza virus infection between 1 January 2016 and 30 June 2023 in Hong Kong. The in-patient mortality, severe respiratory failure (SRF), secondary bacterial pneumonia and acute kidney injury (AKI) were compared. The association between multi-morbidities as reflected by CCI and severe in-hospital outcomes among adult patients hospitalized for rhinovirus infections was also assessed. A total of 41,206 and 2,222 patients were hospitalized for influenza and rhinovirus infections, respectively. Patients with rhinovirus infection showed a significantly higher risk of SRF, secondary bacterial pneumonia and AKI compared to those with seasonal influenza ( P <0.001 for all). Higher CCI (as both continuous variables, by grading as well as cut-off identified by receiver operating characteristic curve analysis) was associated with increased risks of severe in-hospital outcomes. Adults hospitalized for rhinovirus infection were associated with a significantly increased risk of adverse respiratory and kidney outcomes compared with those with seasonal influenza. More medical comorbidities, as reflected by CCI, were shown to be associated with an increased risk of severe in-hospital outcomes.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the knowledge gap regarding the severity of rhinovirus infections compared to seasonal influenza, as rhinovirus was previously thought to cause only mild illnesses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a territory-wide retrospective analysis of adults hospitalized for rhinovirus or influenza virus infection between 1 January 2016 and 30 June 2023 in Hong Kong, with a focus on comparing outcomes between the two groups.
analysis.methods: A retrospective study was conducted using hospital records of adults hospitalized for rhinovirus or influenza virus infection, with outcomes including in-patient mortality, severe respiratory failure, secondary bacterial pneumonia, and acute kidney injury assessed.
analysis.main_results: Adults hospitalized for rhinovirus infection had a significantly increased risk of adverse respiratory and kidney outcomes compared to those with seasonal influenza (P <0.001 for all). Higher Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) scores were associated with increased risks of severe in-hospital outcomes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight that rhinovirus infections can lead to severe in-hospital outcomes, and the presence of multiple comorbidities, as measured by CCI, is a strong predictor of these outcomes in adult patients.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results inform the need for improved surveillance and targeted interventions for rhinovirus infections, particularly in adults with multiple comorbidities, to reduce the risk of severe adverse outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the large sample size and clear association between CCI and severe outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the severity of rhinovirus infections in adults hospitalized between 2016 and 2023 in Hong Kong, comparing outcomes with those of seasonal influenza. It found that rhinovirus infections were associated with significantly higher risks of severe respiratory failure, secondary bacterial pneumonia, and acute kidney injury compared to influenza. The Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) was shown to be a strong predictor of severe outcomes in rhinovirus-infected patients. These findings emphasize the importance of recognizing rhinovirus as a potential cause of serious illness and suggest that comorbidity assessment could aid in risk prediction. The study's retrospective nature and potential for confounding factors limit its evidence strength, though the large sample size and clear associations support its conclusions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在填补关于鼻病毒感染与季节性流感感染严重程度的知识空白,因为鼻病毒此前被认为仅引起轻微疾病。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项针对香港2016年1月1日至2023年6月30日期间因鼻病毒或流感病毒感染住院的成年人的全地区回顾性分析,重点是比较这两个群体的结局。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究使用了因鼻病毒或流感病毒感染住院的成年人的医院记录,评估了住院期间的死亡率、严重呼吸衰竭、继发性细菌性肺炎和急性肾损伤等结局。
elements_zh.main_results: 与季节性流感患者相比,因鼻病毒感染住院的成年人出现不良呼吸和肾脏结局的风险显著增加(所有P值均<0.001)。较高的Charlson合并症指数(CCI)评分与严重住院结局的风险增加相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,鼻病毒感染可能导致严重的住院结局,并且以CCI衡量的多种合并症是成人患者中这些结局的强预测因素。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果强调了需要改进监测以及针对鼻病毒感染的特定干预措施,特别是对于有多种合并症的成年人,以降低严重不良结局的风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其回顾性设计以及潜在的混杂因素,但由于样本量大且CCI与严重结局之间有明确关联,证据是强有力的。

title_zh: 一项针对因鼻病毒感染住院的成年人的全地区研究 – 死亡率,严重不良呼吸和肾脏结局及其与多种合并症的关系
source_body_en: While rhinovirus was thought to cause mild infections such as the common cold, severe infections such as community-acquired pneumonia and asthma exacerbations can also occur. Children with chronic medical conditions have been shown to have increased risks of severe infections. Hypothesis/Gap statement. There is a difference in the risks of serious in-hospital outcomes among adults hospitalized for rhinovirus or influenza virus infection. Multiple morbidities in adult patients are associated with severe infections among patients hospitalized for rhinovirus infections. To compare the risks of serious in-hospital outcomes among adults hospitalized for rhinovirus or influenza virus infection and assess the association between multiple morbidities as represented by Charlson comorbidity index (CCI) in predicting risks of severe infections among patients hospitalized for rhinovirus infections. We conducted a territory-wide retrospective study on adults hospitalized for rhinovirus or influenza virus infection between 1 January 2016 and 30 June 2023 in Hong Kong. The in-patient mortality, severe respiratory failure (SRF), secondary bacterial pneumonia and acute kidney injury (AKI) were compared. The association between multi-morbidities as reflected by CCI and severe in-hospital outcomes among adult patients hospitalized for rhinovirus infections was also assessed. A total of 41,206 and 2,222 patients were hospitalized for influenza and rhinovirus infections, respectively. Patients with rhinovirus infection showed a significantly higher risk of SRF, secondary bacterial pneumonia and AKI compared to those with seasonal influenza ( P <0.001 for all). Higher CCI (as both continuous variables, by grading as well as cut-off identified by receiver operating characteristic curve analysis) was associated with increased risks of severe in-hospital outcomes. Adults hospitalized for rhinovirus infection were associated with a significantly increased risk of adverse respiratory and kidney outcomes compared with those with seasonal influenza. More medical comorbidities, as reflected by CCI, were shown to be associated with an increased risk of severe in-hospital outcomes.
abstract_zh: 尽管鼻病毒被认为会引起轻微感染,如普通感冒,但也可能引发严重感染,如社区获得性肺炎和哮喘加重。患有慢性医疗状况的儿童已被证明更容易发生严重感染。假设/研究空白陈述。因鼻病毒或流感病毒感染住院的成年人之间,严重住院结局的风险存在差异。在因鼻病毒感染住院的成人患者中,多种合并症与严重感染相关。本研究旨在比较因鼻病毒或流感病毒感染住院的成年人的严重住院结局风险,并评估以Charlson合并症指数(CCI)为代表的多种合并症在预测因鼻病毒感染住院患者严重感染风险中的关联。我们对香港2016年1月1日至2023年6月30日期间因鼻病毒或流感病毒感染住院的成年人进行了全地区回顾性研究。比较了住院期间的死亡率、严重呼吸衰竭(SRF)、继发性细菌性肺炎和急性肾损伤(AKI)。还评估了以CCI反映的多种合并症与因鼻病毒感染住院的成人患者严重住院结局之间的关联。总共41,206名患者因流感感染住院,2,222名患者因鼻病毒感染住院。与季节性流感患者相比,鼻病毒感染患者出现严重呼吸衰竭、继发性细菌性肺炎和急性肾损伤的风险显著更高(所有P值均<0.001)。较高的CCI(作为连续变量,通过分级以及通过接受者操作特征曲线分析确定的截断值)与严重住院结局的风险增加相关。与季节性流感患者相比,因鼻病毒感染住院的成年人出现不良呼吸和肾脏结局的风险显著增加。以CCI反映的更多医疗合并症被证明与严重住院结局的风险增加相关。
summary_zh: 尽管鼻病毒被认为会引起轻微感染,如普通感冒,但也可能引发严重感染,如社区获得性肺炎和哮喘加重。患有慢性医疗状况的儿童已被证明更容易发生严重感染。假设/研究空白陈述。因鼻病毒或流感病毒感染住院的成年人之间,严重住院结局的风险存在差异。在因鼻病毒感染住院的成人患者中,多种合并症与严重感染相关。本研究旨在比较因鼻病毒或流感病毒感染住院的成年人的严重住院结局风险,并评估以Charlson合并症指数(CCI)为代表的多种合并症在预测因鼻病毒感染住院患者严重感染风险中的关联。我们对香港2016年1月1日至2023年6月30日期间因鼻病毒或流感病毒感染住院的成年人进行了全地区回顾性研究。比较了住院期间的死亡率、严重呼吸衰竭(SRF)、继发性细菌性肺炎和急性肾损伤(AKI)。还评估了以CCI反映的多种合并症与因鼻病毒感染住院的成人患者严重住院结局之间的关联。总共41,206名患者因流感感染住院,2,222名患者因鼻病毒感染住院。与季节性流感患者相比,鼻病毒感染患者出现严重呼吸衰竭、继发性细菌性肺炎和急性肾损伤的风险显著更高(所有P值均<0.001)。较高的CCI(作为连续变量,通过分级以及通过接受者操作特征曲线分析确定的截断值)与严重住院结局的风险增加相关。与季节性流感患者相比,因鼻病毒感染住院的成年人出现不良呼吸和肾脏结局的风险显著增加。以CCI反映的更多医疗合并症被证明与严重住院结局的风险增加相关。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在填补关于鼻病毒感染与季节性流感感染严重程度的知识空白,因为鼻病毒此前被认为仅引起轻微疾病。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项针对香港2016年1月1日至2023年6月30日期间因鼻病毒或流感病毒感染住院的成年人的全地区回顾性分析,重点是比较这两个群体的结局。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究使用了因鼻病毒或流感病毒感染住院的成年人的医院记录,评估了住院期间的死亡率、严重呼吸衰竭、继发性细菌性肺炎和急性肾损伤等结局。
analysis_zh.main_results: 与季节性流感患者相比,因鼻病毒感染住院的成年人出现不良呼吸和肾脏结局的风险显著增加(所有P值均<0.001)。较高的Charlson合并症指数(CCI)评分与严重住院结局的风险增加相关。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,鼻病毒感染可能导致严重的住院结局,并且以CCI衡量的多种合并症是成人患者中这些结局的强预测因素。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果强调了需要改进监测以及针对鼻病毒感染的特定干预措施,特别是对于有多种合并症的成年人,以降低严重不良结局的风险。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其回顾性设计以及潜在的混杂因素,但由于样本量大且CCI与严重结局之间有明确关联,证据是强有力的。

title: A modelling challenge to improve preparedness for highly pathogenic avian influenza epidemics: objectives, design and synthetic data generation
abstract: Abstract Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) is among the most significant disease threats to poultry worldwide. Modelling challenges, where independent teams address a common epidemiological scenario, can support the development of response capabilities and strengthen communication between modellers and risk managers. Despite the established benefits of these exercises, they remain uncommon in animal health, and none have previously addressed avian influenza. Here Jolly Island, an artificial landscape of 9160 poultry farms with five production types, was developed and seeded with stochastic HPAI epidemics that ran their course over a three-to-four month period. From January through April 2026, 45 registered teams across five continents investigated a selected synthetic epidemic, producing probabilistic forecasts, inferring transmission drivers, and evaluating counterfactual control policies. title: An adenovirus-based mucosal vaccine induces cross-neutralizing antibodies and protects against lethal H5N1 infection in ferrets
abstract: Background H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) has been detected in multiple animal species, including humans, posing a significant threat to public health. Vaccines capable of eliciting robust mucosal and systemic immunity are needed to protect against HPAI infection. Methods First- and second-generation non-replicating adenovirus type-5 vectored vaccines expressing hemagglutinin (HA) from clade 2.1.3.2 (ND1.1) and clade 2.3.4.4b (VXA-H5-02), were administered via peroral route to ferrets. Mucosal and systemic immunogenicity were evaluated. Protective efficacy, viral burden, and shedding was assessed against clade 2.3.4.4b challenge, for clade-matched VXA-H5–02 and clade-mismatched ND1.1 vaccines. Results Immunization elicited mucosal immunity and serum neutralizing activity in ferrets against homologous and heterologous clades. All control animals rapidly succumbed to the lethal 2.3.4.4b clade challenge, compared with survival rates of 38% and 100% in the ND1.1 and VXA-H5–02 vaccine groups, respectively. VXA-H5–02 immunization significantly reduced illness, viral burden, and shedding. Conclusion Second-generation VXA-H5–02 is a promising vaccine candidate capable of inducing systemic and mucosal immunity, offering broad protection against HPAI.

title: Descriptive analysis of dairy cow imports from the United States into Ontario, Canada between 2009 and 2019: implications for the risk of H5N1 introduction
abstract: Since first being identified in March 2024, infections of highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1) have been reported in over one thousand dairy herds in the United States. Canadian dairy cattle have remained free from H5N1 infection, due in part to the testing regulations for interstate and international dairy cow movements. To better understand the trends in historical dairy cow importing patterns and the subsequent potential for H5N1 introduction into Ontario, Canada, we present a descriptive analysis of dairy cow imports from the United States into Ontario dairy herds enrolled in Lactanet Canada services. Between 2009 and 2019, a total of 6,145 dairy cows were imported into 735 Lactanet-enrolled herds. Imports peaked during summer and early fall, with imports spiking at the beginning of each month. Annually, most Lactanet dairy herds did not import any dairy cows. While the total annual number of dairy cow movements decreased between 2014 and 2018, the proportion of dairy cow movements within Ontario made up of imports increased over time. The regional distribution of imported cows was similar to the distribution of Lactanet herds, mostly being concentrated in western and eastern Ontario. However, when considering the density of Lactanet herds, there were disproportionately more imports per herd in southern Ontario. Outgoing infection chains (OIC) of importing herds were mostly short, suggesting that for most herds that imported dairy cows, there were no subsequent domestic movements to other Ontario dairy herds in the calendar year. Mean OIC values were skewed by several importing herds with very large OICs, connecting a large number of herds across all regions of the province. Relative to the network of domestic dairy cow movements, imports from the United States were relatively uncommon and largely clustered in southwest and eastern Ontario. Importing appeared to be seasonal, peaking during late summer and early fall. Outgoing infection chains identified that most herds that import dairy cows do not subsequently move cows to other Ontario-based dairy herds. However, for a few herds, the chain formed by time- and direction-respecting movements had the potential to reach many non-importing herds across the province.

full_text: Influenza A virus (IAV) infection during pregnancy is associated with stillbirth and preterm birth. We hypothesized that maternal IAV infection disrupts placental and fetal immune networks in ways that correlate with disease severity. Pregnant pigtail macaques were inoculated with IAV [A/California/07/2009 (H1N1)] and underwent delivery and fetal necropsy 5 days postinfection (N = 11), with comparison to uninfected controls (N = 16). Stillbirth occurred in 18% of infected pregnancies and in no controls. Although vertical transmission was not observed, low levels of viral RNA were detected in two placentas. Maternal infection was associated with induction of a type I interferon response in the placenta and altered innate and adaptive immune cell populations in the fetus. Maternal disease metrics (e.g., lung viral load and interferon-α) were rarely associated with placental immune perturbations but frequently linked to fetal immune cell populations (CD4+ and CD8+ T cells and monocyte subsets). Collectively, these data indicate that maternal IAV disease severity is associated with dysregulated fetal immunity. MATERIALS AND METHODSStudy designTwo groups of female pigtail macaques (M. nemestrina) were inoculated using a combination of intranasal, intratracheal, intraocular, and intraoral routes with 107.4 PFU of IAV [A/California/07/2009 (H1N1)], reflecting a dosing method previously used in a study of cynomolgus macaques (Macaca fascicularis), which resulted in a productive infection (66). Experimental groups consisted of IAV H1N1–infected pregnant (N = 11) and uninfected pregnant controls (N = 16; table S1). IAV inoculation occurred in the early third trimester to model the time in pregnancy when IAV H1N1 infections are thought to produce the greatest maternal lung disease and pregnancy complications (13, 14). Uninfected controls in this study consisted of pregnant adult pigtail macaques used in prior published studies from two cohorts: (i) control studies catheterizing the amniotic cavity and inoculating saline into the choriodecidual space and/or amniotic fluid; (ii) control studies inoculating medium subcutaneously to mimic procedures in a Zika virus experimental cohort (35, 36). Ethical constraints limit the availability of large, dedicated control cohorts for each experimental study. Thus, historical controls were used with consistent husbandry conditions, necropsy and processing protocols, and experimental protocols to minimize potential confounding variables. Animals in the WaNPRC were not exposed to seasonal IAV infections and thus do not have preexisting immunity to IAV.Ethics statement and animal careAll animal experiments used in this study were approved by the University of Washington Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (protocol# 4165-03, last approved 22 July 2025) and in compliance with the US Department of Health and Human Services Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals and Animal Welfare Act. All animal experiments were performed at the WaNPRC.Macaques inoculated with IAV were observed daily for clinical symptoms of influenza disease, which were scored on a three-point scale to reflect responsiveness of the animal, nasal or ocular discharge, cough, respiratory effort, food consumption, and fecal consistency; higher scores reflected disease, with a 0 in each category indicating a normal assessment. We chose a predefined study end point of 5 dpi to capture immune responses near the expected peak of disease (67, 68). A Cesarean section was performed at the end point, and placentas were extracted to sample chorionic villous tissue. The dam was euthanized using a barbiturate overdose while under anesthesia. The fetus was euthanized using a barbiturate overdose, followed by exsanguination. These methods are approved by the 2007 American Veterinary Medical Association Guidelines on Euthanasia. Necropsies were performed on both the dam and the fetus to obtain samples for transcriptomics, immune assays, and histopathology. Random sections of the placental membrane, chorionic disc, and umbilical cord were evaluated for pathology. In one stillbirth case, FLU9, the fetus was 1 to 2 days postmortem at the time of Cesarean section. Pathologists reported that severe autolysis of the tissue had occurred. Samples were not collected from the fetus because the tissue quality would likely be too low to perform meaningful assays.IAV H1N1 virus cultivation and quantificationWe used an IAV strain [A/California/07/2009 H1N1 influenza virus (CA09)] that was obtained from the World Reference Center for Emerging Viruses and Arboviruses at the University of Texas Medical Branch at Galveston. Before culturing the virus, Madin-Darby canine kidney (MDCK) cells (American Type Culture Collection, Manassas, VA, USA) were cultured in Dulbecco’s modified Eagle’s medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum, 25 mM Hepes, penicillin (100 U/ml), and streptomycin (100 μg/ml). Cells were incubated at 37°C and 5% CO2 and confirmed to be free of mycoplasma with the MycoAlert mycoplasma detection kit (LT07-318, Lonza) before use for virus cultivation. Subconfluent monolayers of MDCK cells in T150 flasks were washed with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) and infected at a multiplicity of infection of 0.5 (5 ml of serum-free minimum essential medium) at 37°C and 5% CO2. After 1 hour, the medium was removed, cells were washed with 1× PBS, and the medium was replaced. The supernatant was harvested after 36 hours and centrifuged at room temperature to remove cellular debris (1800 rpm for 5 min, followed by 3000 rpm for 10 min). Virus stock was frozen at −80°C. The viral titer of each stock was quantified using a median tissue culture infectious dose (TCID50) assay with hemagglutination readout and converted to PFU per milliliter (69). To transform TCID50 per milliliter into PFU per milliliter, TCID50 per milliliter was multiplied by 0.7. Reagents were obtained from Thermo Fisher Scientific unless otherwise stated (Waltham, MA).RNA isolation and RT-qPCRTissue samples were kept in RNAlater Stabilization Solution (#15596018, Thermo Fisher Scientific) before homogenization in Precellys homogenizing tubes (#1011152, Cayman Chemical, Ann Arbor, MI, USA) with the Precellys Evolution machine (Bertin Technologies, Montigny-le-Bretonneux, France). RNA was extracted from homogenates using the RNeasy Mini Kit (#74106, QIAGEN) and treated with deoxyribonuclease (#79256, QIAGEN). RNA was quantified using the NanoDrop 2000 spectrophotometer (#ND-2000, Thermo Fisher Scientific) and the Qubit 4 fluorometer (#Q33238, Invitrogen). RNA quality was evaluated by measuring the RNA integrity number (RIN) with the 4200 TapeStation System (#G2991BA, Agilent).To quantify IAV vRNA levels from different sample origins, we used RT-qPCR and a WHO-approved primer/probe set (70). cDNA was generated from RNA isolates using an iScript Select cDNA synthesis kit (#1708897, Bio-Rad) using H1N1 HA-specific forward primer following the manufacturer’s instructions. qPCR was done with H1N1 HA-specific primers and probes (forward, GGGTAGCCCCATTGCAT; reverse, AGAGTGATTCACACTCTGGATTTC; probe: 5′-[FAM] TGGGTAAATGTAACATTGCTGGCTGG [TAMRA]-3′) using the TaqMan Fast Advanced Master Mix (#444964, Thermo Fisher Scientific) and a QuantStudio 3 machine (#A28132, Thermo Fisher Scientific) following the manufacturer’s instructions. Samples were run in triplicate.An external plasmid standard curve was used to determine vRNA quantities with the lower limit of quantification being three copies per reaction. A negative control with no template added was used to assess the possibility of contamination. Amplification was defined as fluorescent activity exceeding a threshold of 0.1. Negative results were defined as any sample that did not amplify or had a Ct value greater than 38 cycles. Positive results were defined as any amplified sample with a Ct value less than 38 cycles for all three replicates. Samples with low positive results (Ct > 35) had RNA reextracted from a new sample aliquot, and RT-qPCR was run two more times in triplicate to verify results, totaling nine replicates. Copies of vRNA per milligram of tissue were calculated on the basis of tissue weight, RNA concentration, RNA volume, and volume of cDNA sample input.Cytokine quantificationProcartaPlex NHP multiplex kits were used to quantify cytokines from lysates or fluids (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Tissue lysis and homogenization were performed using an Invitrogen ProcartaPlex Cell Lysis Buffer (#EPX-99999-000, Thermo Fisher Scientific) with the addition of a protease inhibitor cocktail (#PI78430, Thermo Fisher Scientific) using the Precellys Evolution system, as previously described. Type I IFNs (IFN-α and IFN-β) were quantified using the cynomolgus IFN-β and cynomolgus/rhesus IFN-α enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) kits (#46415-1 and #46100-1, respectively, PBL Biosciences, Menlo Park, CA, USA). All protocols followed the manufacturer’s guidelines. The Luminex analysis software estimated cytokine concentrations that fell outside the range of the standard curve.ImmunophenotypingImmunophenotyping by flow cytometry was performed to determine the frequencies of immune cells in the placenta and fetal lung, mesenteric fetal lymph node, and fetal blood. Tissues from the placental disc and fetal organs were dissociated into single-cell suspensions and assessed for viability using acridine orange/propidium iodide (Nexcelom Bioscience LLC). Then, samples were stained with a panel of antibodies in Brilliant Stain Buffer (BD Biosciences) for 20 min to identify immune cells as previously described (71). Antibodies used included BD Biosciences: CD3 (SP34-2)–BV650, CD8 (RPA-T8)–BUV395, CD11b (ICRF44)–APC–Cy7, CD11c (SHCL-3)–phycoerythrin (PE), CD45 (D058-1283)–PE–CF594, CD86 (IT2.2)–PE–Cy5, and γδ T cell receptor (B1)–fluorescein isothiocyanate; BioLegend: CD4 (OKT4)–BV605, CD14 (M5E2)–BV785, CD16 (3G8)–Alexa Flour 700, CD20 (2H7)–BV570, and human leukocyte antigen–DR (L243)–BV711; Invitrogen: CD123 (6H6)–eFlour 450 and LIVE/DEAD Fixable Aqua for 405-nm excitation; Beckman Coulter: CD159a (Z199)–PC7; and Miltenyi: CD66 (TET2)–APC. The staining protocol proceeded in three steps: LIVE/DEAD Fixable Aqua, then all antibodies other than CD11c and CD123, and lastly CD11c and CD123. After staining, samples were fixed with 1% paraformaldehyde and analyzed on a Symphony A3 flow cytometer (BD Biosciences) using FACS Diva 8 software (BD Biosciences). Samples were analyzed using FlowJo 10.9.0 (FlowJo LLC). All events were initially gated on forward scatter (FSC) singlets, CD45+ leukocytes, live cells, and then on FSC-A and side scatter–A profiles. Populations were defined using canonical markers as described in table S5. Representative gating strategies are shown for granulocytes (fig. S18), lymphoid cells (fig. S19), and monocytes (fig. S20). Populations were excluded from analysis if they did not meet the minimum threshold of >100 cells in their parent gate.Total RNA-seq library preparation and analysisTotal RNA-seq was performed on chorionic villous tissue from the placenta. We used 100 ng of RNA with RIN > 3 as input for RNA library prep using the KAPA RNA HyperPrep kit with RiboErase HMR (#08098131702, Roche Diagnostics Corporation, Indianapolis, IN, USA). The kit was not only designed for human, mouse, and rat samples but also effectively reduced ribosomal RNA in our NHP RNA isolates. Libraries were prepared following the manufacturer’s standard protocol. Library quantity and quality were evaluated using Qubit Fluorometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and TapeStation (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA, USA). Constructed libraries were sequenced on the NovaSeq 6000 Sequencing System (#20012850, Illumina, San Diego, CA, USA), which produced 2 × 100 nucleotide-stranded paired-end reads.Raw sequences were aligned to the M. nemestrina reference genome from Ensembl (Mnem_1.0, INSDC Assembly GCA_000956065.1) using STAR in Partek Flow, a bioinformatics software suite (Partek, Chesterfield, MO, USA). Ensembl gene symbol conversions were used to ensure consistency across all gene IDs. As the quality score was greater than 35 across all samples, no bases were trimmed, and 100% of sequencing bases overlapped with read lengths of the reference genome. The raw count matrix was downloaded from Partek. Subsequent statistical processing and analysis of count data were performed within the R statistical computing environment (R version 4.4.0). Gene counts were filtered by a row mean of 10 or greater, then normalized using edgeR to implement TMM normalization. Counts were transformed into log2 counts using voom, a function in the limma package that modifies RNA-seq data to create a normalized count matrix (72, 73). Differential expression (DE) analysis compared placental samples from IAV-infected animals with those from uninfected controls. Comparisons were based on a linear model fit for each gene using limma. The criteria for all DE analyses were an absolute fold change of 2 and a P < 0.05. Adjusted P values were calculated using the Benjamini-Hochberg method to reduce the false discovery rate (FDR). Gene set enrichment analysis was conducted across the comparison group using fgsea with the Broad Institute Molecular Signatures database (74).Hierarchical clustering analysis, an unsupervised machine learning approach, was performed to group total RNA-seq profiles based on their similarity in Euclidean distance using the hclust function in R. Ward’s linkage was used to minimize variance within each cluster. The optimal number of clusters was determined using the elbow method. The resulting hierarchy was visualized using a dendrogram. Last, an ORA was performed to determine if predefined sets of genes in GO pathways were enriched in the cluster of differentially expressed genes obtained from the hierarchical clustering analysis using the clusterProfiler package in R.NanoString nCounterTo validate our results from bulk RNA-seq, we chose a quantitative multiplex method of direct digital counting of gene transcripts using the NanoString nCounter Analysis Systems (NanoString Technologies Inc., Seattle, WA, USA). RNA extracted from the chorionic villous tissues of the placenta was analyzed using the NanoString nCounter NHP Immunology V2 gene expression code set (#11500276, NanoString Technologies Inc.). RNA hybridization reactions were performed according to the manufacturer’s protocol. Probe-target RNA complexes from all reactions were processed and immobilized on nCounter cartridges using the nCounter Prep Station. Gene transcripts were quantified with the nCounter Digital Analyzer (#MAN-C0035-07, NanoString Technologies Inc).Statistical analysesAll statistical analyses were performed in RStudio (using R version 4.4.0) or nSolver (nCounter data only), both of which use the R programming language. A P value of less than 0.05 was considered significant, and that of 0.05 to 0.1 was reported considering the modest sample size. Pearson’s correlation coefficient was used to calculate correlations between two variables using unadjusted P values. Data visualizations were done using ggplot2, ggpmisc, and ComplexHeatmaps packages and their derivatives (75, 76). full_text_sections.abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) infection during pregnancy is associated with stillbirth and preterm birth. We hypothesized that maternal IAV infection disrupts placental and fetal immune networks in ways that correlate with disease severity. Pregnant pigtail macaques were inoculated with IAV [A/California/07/2009 (H1N1)] and underwent delivery and fetal necropsy 5 days postinfection (N = 11), with comparison to uninfected controls (N = 16). Stillbirth occurred in 18% of infected pregnancies and in no controls. Although vertical transmission was not observed, low levels of viral RNA were detected in two placentas. Maternal infection was associated with induction of a type I interferon response in the placenta and altered innate and adaptive immune cell populations in the fetus. Maternal disease metrics (e.g., lung viral load and interferon-α) were rarely associated with placental immune perturbations but frequently linked to fetal immune cell populations (CD4+ and CD8+ T cells and monocyte subsets). Collectively, these data indicate that maternal IAV disease severity is associated with dysregulated fetal immunity.
full_text_sections.methods: MATERIALS AND METHODSStudy designTwo groups of female pigtail macaques (M. nemestrina) were inoculated using a combination of intranasal, intratracheal, intraocular, and intraoral routes with 107.4 PFU of IAV [A/California/07/2009 (H1N1)], reflecting a dosing method previously used in a study of cynomolgus macaques (Macaca fascicularis), which resulted in a productive infection (66). Experimental groups consisted of IAV H1N1–infected pregnant (N = 11) and uninfected pregnant controls (N = 16; table S1). IAV inoculation occurred in the early third trimester to model the time in pregnancy when IAV H1N1 infections are thought to produce the greatest maternal lung disease and pregnancy complications (13, 14). Uninfected controls in this study consisted of pregnant adult pigtail macaques used in prior published studies from two cohorts: (i) control studies catheterizing the amniotic cavity and inoculating saline into the choriodecidual space and/or amniotic fluid; (ii) control studies inoculating medium subcutaneously to mimic procedures in a Zika virus experimental cohort (35, 36). Ethical constraints limit the availability of large, dedicated control cohorts for each experimental study. Thus, historical controls were used with consistent husbandry conditions, necropsy and processing protocols, and experimental protocols to minimize potential confounding variables. Animals in the WaNPRC were not exposed to seasonal IAV infections and thus do not have preexisting immunity to IAV.Ethics statement and animal careAll animal experiments used in this study were approved by the University of Washington Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (protocol# 4165-03, last approved 22 July 2025) and in compliance with the US Department of Health and Human Services Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals and Animal Welfare Act. All animal experiments were performed at the WaNPRC.Macaques inoculated with IAV were observed daily for clinical symptoms of influenza disease, which were scored on a three-point scale to reflect responsiveness of the animal, nasal or ocular discharge, cough, respiratory effort, food consumption, and fecal consistency; higher scores reflected disease, with a 0 in each category indicating a normal assessment. We chose a predefined study end point of 5 dpi to capture immune responses near the expected peak of disease (67, 68). A Cesarean section was performed at the end point, and placentas were extracted to sample chorionic villous tissue. The dam was euthanized using a barbiturate overdose while under anesthesia. The fetus was euthanized using a barbiturate overdose, followed by exsanguination. These methods are approved by the 2007 American Veterinary Medical Association Guidelines on Euthanasia. Necropsies were performed on both the dam and the fetus to obtain samples for transcriptomics, immune assays, and histopathology. Random sections of the placental membrane, chorionic disc, and umbilical cord were evaluated for pathology. In one stillbirth case, FLU9, the fetus was 1 to 2 days postmortem at the time of Cesarean section. Pathologists reported that severe autolysis of the tissue had occurred. Samples were not collected from the fetus because the tissue quality would likely be too low to perform meaningful assays.IAV H1N1 virus cultivation and quantificationWe used an IAV strain [A/California/07/2009 H1N1 influenza virus (CA09)] that was obtained from the World Reference Center for Emerging Viruses and Arboviruses at the University of Texas Medical Branch at Galveston. Before culturing the virus, Madin-Darby canine kidney (MDCK) cells (American Type Culture Collection, Manassas, VA, USA) were cultured in Dulbecco’s modified Eagle’s medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum, 25 mM Hepes, penicillin (100 U/ml), and streptomycin (100 μg/ml). Cells were incubated at 37°C and 5% CO2 and confirmed to be free of mycoplasma with the MycoAlert mycoplasma detection kit (LT07-318, Lonza) before use for virus cultivation. Subconfluent monolayers of MDCK cells in T150 flasks were washed with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) and infected at a multiplicity of infection of 0.5 (5 ml of serum-free minimum essential medium) at 37°C and 5% CO2. After 1 hour, the medium was removed, cells were washed with 1× PBS, and the medium was replaced. The supernatant was harvested after 36 hours and centrifuged at room temperature to remove cellular debris (1800 rpm for 5 min, followed by 3000 rpm for 10 min). Virus stock was frozen at −80°C. The viral titer of each stock was quantified using a median tissue culture infectious dose (TCID50) assay with hemagglutination readout and converted to PFU per milliliter (69). To transform TCID50 per milliliter into PFU per milliliter, TCID50 per milliliter was multiplied by 0.7. Reagents were obtained from Thermo Fisher Scientific unless otherwise stated (Waltham, MA).RNA isolation and RT-qPCRTissue samples were kept in RNAlater Stabilization Solution (#15596018, Thermo Fisher Scientific) before homogenization in Precellys homogenizing tubes (#1011152, Cayman Chemical, Ann Arbor, MI, USA) with the Precellys Evolution machine (Bertin Technologies, Montigny-le-Bretonneux, France). RNA was extracted from homogenates using the RNeasy Mini Kit (#74106, QIAGEN) and treated with deoxyribonuclease (#79256, QIAGEN). RNA was quantified using the NanoDrop 2000 spectrophotometer (#ND-2000, Thermo Fisher Scientific) and the Qubit 4 fluorometer (#Q33238, Invitrogen). RNA quality was evaluated by measuring the RNA integrity number (RIN) with the 4200 TapeStation System (#G2991BA, Agilent).To quantify IAV vRNA levels from different sample origins, we used RT-qPCR and a WHO-approved primer/probe set (70). cDNA was generated from RNA isolates using an iScript Select cDNA synthesis kit (#1708897, Bio-Rad) using H1N1 HA-specific forward primer following the manufacturer’s instructions. qPCR was done with H1N1 HA-specific primers and probes (forward, GGGTAGCCCCATTGCAT; reverse, AGAGTGATTCACACTCTGGATTTC; probe: 5′-[FAM] TGGGTAAATGTAACATTGCTGGCTGG [TAMRA]-3′) using the TaqMan Fast Advanced Master Mix (#444964, Thermo Fisher Scientific) and a QuantStudio 3 machine (#A28132, Thermo Fisher Scientific) following the manufacturer’s instructions. Samples were run in triplicate.An external plasmid standard curve was used to determine vRNA quantities with the lower limit of quantification being three copies per reaction. A negative control with no template added was used to assess the possibility of contamination. Amplification was defined as fluorescent activity exceeding a threshold of 0.1. Negative results were defined as any sample that did not amplify or had a Ct value greater than 38 cycles. Positive results were defined as any amplified sample with a Ct value less than 38 cycles for all three replicates. Samples with low positive results (Ct > 35) had RNA reextracted from a new sample aliquot, and RT-qPCR was run two more times in triplicate to verify results, totaling nine replicates. Copies of vRNA per milligram of tissue were calculated on the basis of tissue weight, RNA concentration, RNA volume, and volume of cDNA sample input.Cytokine quantificationProcartaPlex NHP multiplex kits were used to quantify cytokines from lysates or fluids (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Tissue lysis and homogenization were performed using an Invitrogen ProcartaPlex Cell Lysis Buffer (#EPX-99999-000, Thermo Fisher Scientific) with the addition of a protease inhibitor cocktail (#PI78430, Thermo Fisher Scientific) using the Precellys Evolution system, as previously described. Type I IFNs (IFN-α and IFN-β) were quantified using the cynomolgus IFN-β and cynomolgus/rhesus IFN-α enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) kits (#46415-1 and #46100-1, respectively, PBL Biosciences, Menlo Park, CA, USA). Results were compared to 16 historical control uninfected pregnant pigtail macaques (CTRL cohort; table S1), which received either subcutaneous medium inoculations (N = 9) (35) or saline inoculation into the choriodecidual space via catheters (N = 7) (36) for comparison against Zika virus or group B Streptococcus cohorts, respectively. For the FLU cohort, a Cesarean section and necropsies of the dam and fetus were performed 5 days after inoculation. For the CTRL cohort, the interval between inoculation and Cesarean section varied depending on the intended purpose of the design, ranging between 1 and 100 days (table S1). Animals that exhibited the most severe disease based on clinical scores were FLU8 and FLU9; of these animals, FLU9 experienced a stillbirth. Clinical scores were highest between day 3 and day 5 postinoculation. Uninfected CTRL animals did not show signs of respiratory disease.
